questions.key_step: Add the equation to its conjugate to get $\bar z=\pm iz$, then solve two quadratics.
questions.justification: Routine chain: conjugate, add, split into two cases and solve; one known trick but several stages and a check that roots are distinct; options present. Easier than 2023-P1-Q17 (L3).

questions.key_step: Interpret the condition as a margin of at least $k$ cells on every side, then count positions for $k=1,2$.
questions.justification: Short casework with a small interpretation step; no heavy computation and options help. Same demand as 2021-P2-Q1 (routine counting).

questions.key_step: Reduce to permutations with four forbidden fixed points and count by $D_4+D_5$ or inclusion-exclusion.
questions.justification: One standard model (restricted permutation / derangements) with a short case split; the free element f(1) is the only trap and options let the student check. Easier than 2026-P2-Q10 (numerical inclusion-exclusion, L4).

questions.key_step: Sum $\binom{n}{4}$ over all diagonals of length at least $4$, in both directions.
questions.justification: Routine chain: list diagonal lengths, apply C(n,4), double for the other direction; small precision risk (one direction gives the distractor 182) but no new idea. Same demand as 2021-P2-Q1 (L2).

questions.key_step: Use product of divisors $=N^{d(N)/2}$, then compare prime exponents with $24^x$.
questions.justification: One familiar result (product of divisors) followed by a direct exponent comparison; JEE Main level. Close to 2021-P2-Q17 (one standard tool applied once).

questions.key_step: Translate 'no borrowing' into $x_i\le y_i$ per place and multiply, remembering the leading digits are non-zero.
questions.justification: Short routine chain with one interpretation step and a leading-digit trap; options let the student check the pattern. Same demand as 2021-P2-Q1 (L2).

questions.key_step: Use $\binom{20}{k}=\binom{20}{20-k}$ to double the sum into all odd-position coefficients, which total $2^{19}$.
questions.justification: Single familiar symmetry-plus-odd-sum trick, applied once; JEE Main level. Close to 2023-P1-Q13 (L1, binomial coefficient equating).

questions.key_step: Recognise the sum as Vandermonde's identity and equate with the middle coefficient.
questions.justification: Two standard ideas chained (Vandermonde, middle coefficient) with a short finish; options available. Easier than 2025-P2-Q10 (numerical largest coefficient, L4).

questions.key_step: Spot $7^3=1+19\cdot18$ and expand binomially (or use Fermat).
questions.justification: One familiar trick (a power of the base is one more than a multiple of the divisor); JEE Main level with four-option check. Close to 2023-P1-Q13 (L1).

questions.key_step: Recognise the alternating sum as the $x^5$ coefficient of $\left((1+x)^{101}-1\right)^5$.
questions.justification: The key step is an unfamiliar-looking pattern (hidden $(u-1)^5$ with $u=(1+x)^{101}$) that students rarely practise, though the computation after it is one line; options help. Placed between routine L2 and the hidden-structure Leibniz question 2026-P2-Q5 (L4).

questions.key_step: Sum the geometric series $p+q^2p+q^4p+\dots$ for first success on odd throws.
questions.justification: Routine chain: count favourable cases, set up the odd-throw geometric series, simplify and reduce the fraction; no new idea and options present. Easier than 2023-P2-Q2 (L3, toss until two consecutive match).

questions.key_step: Split into primes $2$ and $5$ and count exponent triples under pairwise-maximum conditions ($7\times10$).
questions.justification: Needs a decoupling idea (prime-wise exponents) plus two careful casework counts (one forces C=4); a slip changes the count and one option is 'None of these'. Between routine counting (L2) and 2024-P1-Q11 (L4).

questions.key_step: Expand $(e^x-1)^2=e^{2x}-2e^x+1$ and read the $x^4$ coefficient
questions.justification: One familiar move (exponential series) applied once; no decision beyond squaring. Same one-move character as 2026-P2-Q4 and 2024-P2-Q3.

questions.key_step: Symmetry $i\to n-i$ removes $(i+j)$; then $\sum C_r^2$ and $(\sum C_r)^2$
questions.justification: Non-routine symmetry on a double sum plus two standard identities; but options and an $n=1$ test allow checking, so it stays at 3 rather than 4 (2025-P2-Q10 is a numerical, heavier case).

questions.key_step: Split $1+kx$ and recognise $(1-u)^n$ and the $k\,C_k$ derivative form
questions.justification: Routine chain of standard binomial identities; options are constants so $n=1$ settles it. Comparable to a routine multi-step Level 2 such as 2023-P2-Q9.

questions.key_step: Sum of roots (Vieta) or factor by inspection; real part is additive
questions.justification: One familiar move, no decision; closest to other single-move items like 2025-P1-Q7.

questions.key_step: $a+b=-1$ from the root-of-unity sum, then reduce $ab$ mod 7
questions.justification: Several standard facts chained (sum of roots, expansion of 9 products, reduction), no insight beyond that; routine multi-step.

questions.key_step: $\alpha_k=\alpha_1^k$ so the sum is $(1+\alpha_1)^n-1$
questions.justification: Binomial theorem applied to roots of unity, then rewriting $\alpha_1=\alpha_2/\alpha_1$; short chain, standard idea.

questions.key_step: Dictionary rank by counting words before SIKAR; A.P. iff $a,c$ same parity
questions.justification: Two independent routine counts (rank and A.P. probability) combined into one last-digit answer; no unfamiliar idea, small slip risk, options present.

questions.key_step: $t=z^3$, conjugate roots so $|t|=5$
questions.justification: One substitution then a modulus; single familiar move.

questions.key_step: Split into real and imaginary parts: $x-y=1$ and $x-y=|z|$
questions.justification: One familiar move (write $z=x+iy$) with two linear equations; question text had a typo that was corrected.

questions.key_step: $C_1$ is a parabola, $C_2$ a ray; tangent from $(-1,-1)$ and rejecting the wrong slope
questions.justification: Two ideas linked (complex locus to conic, then tangent through a point with ray-direction check); more than routine but no deep insight. Between 2026-P2-Q2 (L2) and 2023-P2-Q13 (L4).
One familiar move (geometric series then roots of unity) with a small exclusion check.

questions.key_step: Rewrite the sum via dot products and use |a+b+c|^2 >= 0 for the extremum; check it is attainable
questions.justification: One standard identity plus a non-negativity bound, then check attainability (2,3,4 form a triangle); 'None of these' option adds a small trap. Close to the one-trick Level 1 anchor but chain of three short stages puts it at 2.

questions.key_step: k! is divisible by 4 (resp. 3) from k = 4 (resp. 3) on, so all later terms are 1
questions.justification: One observation (factorial divisibility kills the periodicity) followed by routine bookkeeping of the first few terms and counting 97 and 98 ones; counting slip is the only risk.

questions.key_step: Enumerate the product triples and discard the ones using 1 or repeated numbers
questions.justification: Direct enumeration of three triples over a ten-element set; no insight needed beyond excluding 1.

questions.key_step: Turn 'stable' into order constraints and count arrangements by who is rank 3 (middle or corner)
questions.justification: Unfamiliar set-up (poset on a pyramid) and a short case count where overlooking the corner case gives 12/720 = 1/60, not an option, but nearby options exist; two cases, moderate precision risk.

questions.key_step: Real right-hand side forces Im(z^2 - z)=0, i.e. y(2x-1)=0, so z is real
questions.justification: Standard 'expression is real' move, a tidy factorisation using the Re(z) hypothesis, then x^6=64; options are an easy final check. Single concept so no multi-correct floor. Between the Level 1 Apollonius anchor and the Level 3 modulus anchors.

questions.key_step: x^2 - x + 1 = 0 gives x^6 = 1 hence a = 2; then b in {5,7} from the unit-digit cycle of 4^n
questions.justification: Two short, familiar pieces from different chapters (complex roots of unity and unit digits); the multi-correct floor of 2.5 applies. Each piece alone is Level 1-2.

questions.key_step: Each element appears in C(21,10) subsets, so the total is 253 x C(21,10); then test divisibility of C(21,10)
questions.justification: Contribution-of-each-element counting is a known technique but the divisibility checks by 8 and 17 require factorising C(21,10) (Kummer or direct), and four statements each need a verdict; multi-concept so floor 2.5, level 3.

questions.key_step: Place the three required digits in order (5x4x3), then free the other two places with 7 digit choices each
questions.justification: Routine counting once leading zeros are handled; a single slip (e.g. counting 6 positions or 8 free digits) is the only risk. Matches the Level 2 counting anchor.

questions.key_step: Use r -> n-r to get sum r/C(n,r) = (n/2) sum 1/C(n,r), then cancel the positive sum
questions.justification: One familiar symmetry trick followed by a quadratic; short chain. Two standard steps (not a single move) places it at 2.

questions.key_step: G.P. of powers of 2 <=> A.P. of exponents <=> same-parity pair; then split by parity of n
questions.justification: Key recognition (G.P. to A.P. of exponents) then parity casework in two cases with two options to verify each; multi-concept so floor 2.5, rated 3 since two ideas are linked and precision is needed.

questions.key_step: Both equations share root 0, so two solutions iff p/r = q/s; count quadruples and restrict the sample space for Statement II
questions.justification: Two statements each need a careful count over 256 quadruples with ratio grouping; the printed 'exactly one solution' also needs interpreting. Multi-concept floor 2.5; chain of casework gives 3.

questions.key_step: Check pairwise products P(Ei)P(Ej) and the triple product separately (Bernstein-type example)
questions.justification: Textbook Bernstein-type example; a few short probability computations and no insight beyond recalling that pairwise independence is weaker than mutual independence. Single concept, so no floor.

questions.key_step: Know that only square and pentagon have all diagonals equal, and count k(k-3)/2 parity for k = 3..10
questions.justification: Two quick fact-based checks (equal diagonals; parity of diagonal count) over eight polygons; multi-concept floor of 2.5 applies. Each statement is routine, with only the triangle (no diagonals) as a subtle point.

questions.key_step: Median of binomial coefficients is 45; variance >= 0 (Cauchy-Schwarz) gives n >= 16.
questions.justification: Two short, familiar moves (median of a symmetric list, variance non-negative gives n>=16) with four options to check. Closest to 2026-P2-Q12 (L2, mean/variance data). Multi-correct multi-concept floor 2.5 applied (binomial values + statistics).

questions.key_step: Sum zero + fifth-power sum zero => e2 = 0 => differences are z, z*omega, z*omega^2 (equilateral).
questions.justification: Needs the e1=0 power-sum identity (or factorisation) to reach the equilateral conclusion, then four short checks including an orientation subtlety in (B). One non-trivial but practised idea, options help. Near 2021-P1-Q16 and 2023-P1-Q17 (both L3).

questions.key_step: Rationalise f(x), eliminate x to get circle u^2+v^2=v (centre (0,1/2), r=1/2), then hexagon area.
questions.justification: Parametric locus identification (three short steps) then a standard hexagon area; one decisive idea, familiar to well-prepared students. Closest to 2021-P1-Q16 (L3, locus of z given condition).

questions.key_step: Count favourable selections for exactly 5 alike (6C5 x 4 x 3) and 6 alike; A5 and A6 are exclusive.
questions.justification: Routine binomial counting and one observation of exclusivity; options to check. Closest to 2026-P1-Q5 (L2, MCQ on probabilities/conditional).

questions.key_step: Treat each coin independently: eaten with probability 3/4, then binomial with n=4.
questions.justification: One simplifying idea (collapse two rounds into one independent trial) then a short binomial sum; options available. Near 2026-P1-Q5 (L2) and 2021-P2-Q17 (L1).

questions.key_step: Use z z-bar = 1 to show w = -w-bar (purely imaginary, whole y-axis); then identify each option as a locus.
questions.justification: Single standard trick on the unit circle, followed by four locus identifications; (D) degenerate-hyperbola trap requires care and equivalence to the whole axis must be checked. Near 2021-P1-Q16 (L3).

questions.key_step: Equal-length vectors u,v,w with u+v+w=0 force uv+vw+wu=0, which gives (A),(B),(C); angle B gives (D).
questions.justification: Standard equilateral-triangle conditions chained over four statements, no single hard idea. Level 2 (routine multi-step); no equivalence/multi floor needed. Nearest 2025-P1-Q7 (L1) is simpler; this has four checks.

questions.key_step: Roots are 2w, 2w^2 so z/2 is a cube root of unity and terms repeat 1,1,4 with period 3.
questions.justification: Short chain: roots as 2*omega, periodicity of the terms, sum of 30 terms, plus modulus/argument checks; options help decide S>50. Slightly above routine because period-3 pattern must be spotted. Near 2025-P2-Q13 (L4, omega-power sum numerical) but easier as MCQ.

questions.key_step: Write z' = z e^{i alpha}, z'' = z e^{-i alpha} and check each statement directly.
questions.justification: Single familiar rotation fact, four one-line verifications; near-routine but several steps. Nearest 2025-P1-Q7 (L1) is a single move; four statements push to Level 2.

questions.key_step: Symmetry between first n coins of Ram and Shyam; Ram's last coin decides ties (or heads/tails swap).
questions.justification: Classic symmetry result; once seen it is two lines. Statements C, D follow from A. Option-based, familiar to prepared students. Near 2023-P2-Q2 (L3) as probability reasoning, but simpler; rated 2.

questions.key_step: Write P(n) as a telescoping product 1/(n(n+1)) and solve n(n+1)>2010.
questions.justification: Single concept, one telescoping product then a quadratic inequality; routine chain with no insight; four options to check. Nearest anchor 2023-P2-Q2 (stopping rule) was L3 but that needed a recursion; this is simpler.

questions.key_step: Reduce the posterior to 4^m : 2^m 3^(m-10) : 7^(m-10) and compare growth rates for the limits.
questions.justification: Bayes plus binomial likelihood is a familiar Advanced setup (anchors rated 3); four statements each needing a check, and the limits add a second concept, so multi-concept floor 2.5 does not bind above the raw 3.

questions.key_step: Recognise that the referee seeing plus corresponds to an even/odd number of sign changes and apply Bayes.
questions.justification: Bayes with a three-stage chain and four statements to compare; anchors for Bayes (2024-P1-Q2, 2025-P2-Q11) are L3; options let the student check, so not 4.

questions.key_step: Find the real root, then use the vertical side z1z2 and the horizontal distance to z3.
questions.justification: Factorisation of a cubic and a base-height area; several routine steps, no insight, with options. Two chapters (equations, complex geometry) but all routine.

questions.key_step: Place the hexagon with centre at the origin so that alpha, beta, gamma become the cube roots of 8.
questions.justification: Needs a geometric decoding of the hexagon (centre O, radius 2) and then a Vieta/expansion; two chapters, but standard patterns; options available. Similar in spirit to 2026-P1-Q13 (L3).

questions.key_step: Spot that the summand is a difference V(r)-V(r-1) of ratios of binomial coefficients, then evaluate Q by Vandermonde.
questions.justification: The telescoping is non-routine (idea not met in standard practice) and algebra heavy; needs two binomial results. Comparable to the telescoping-product anchor 2026-P1-Q12 (L4).

questions.key_step: Telescoping gives P; the alternating sum of squares of C(100,r) equals C(100,50) because 100/2 is even.
questions.justification: Needs both the telescoping idea (non-routine) and the alternating-squares identity (known but easy to get the sign wrong); each paragraph part rated separately and high. Anchor 2026-P1-Q12 (L4).

questions.key_step: Combine P=C(100,50)-1 with Q=R=C(100,50) to get Q+R=2P+2.
questions.justification: Same heavy machinery as Q52/Q53 (telescoping plus two binomial identities) and the final combination is short; rated 4 like its siblings.

questions.key_step: Convert 'part in the second quadrant' to c-1<=0 for the disc centre (c,1), then solve a quadratic inequality.
questions.justification: Locus reading plus a quadratic inequality; routine chain. The paragraph itself is missing in the PDF and was reconstructed (low confidence in the exact wording).

questions.key_step: Max |z-i| over the family of discs is the distance from i to the farthest disc point, using the minimum -5/4 of the quadratic.
questions.justification: Two ideas linked (minimum of a quadratic and farthest point of a disc) built on the Q55 reading; reconstructed paragraph, so low confidence.

questions.key_step: Identify the extremal point -9/4+i and compute its argument (reference angle is arctan of Im/|Re| = 4/9).
questions.justification: Linked to Q56 (needs the same disc setup), then a short argument computation; the printed key reads the ratio upside down. Reconstructed paragraph, so low confidence.

questions.key_step: Guess probability 1/15 for multi-answer and the unique split 3+3+3+1, then choose questions out of 20
questions.justification: Two ideas linked (non-obvious 1/15 guess probability, hypergeometric choice of questions) with a 'none of these' option; close to Bayes quiz question 2024-P1-Q2 (L3).

questions.key_step: Each element has 4 placements (disjoint), 3 when union is S
questions.justification: One familiar membership-vector count, short; near routine counting anchor 2021-P2-Q1 (L2).

questions.key_step: Common element fixed, others have 7 patterns; B of size 1 means others avoid B (4 patterns)
questions.justification: Two-stage conditional counting with an interpretation trap on 'B exactly 1 element'; slightly above routine paragraph counting 2021-P2-Q1 (L2), near 2024-P1-Q2 (L3).

questions.key_step: 7 patterns per element; A=B leaves 3 patterns
questions.justification: Same method as Q59 once established, one short pattern count; routine like 2021-P2-Q1 (L2).

questions.key_step: Read each arg equation as a ray from a vertex, giving a unit square
questions.justification: One familiar move (rays form a unit square); no computation; compare 2025-P1-Q7 (L1).

questions.key_step: Purely imaginary sum gives Re z2 = -Re z1; solve 12x^4-4x^2-1=0 (or shift to midpoint)
questions.justification: Algebraic chain of three stages (product from sum and sum of squares, real/imag split, biquadratic) with a clean trick; like 2023-P1-Q17 (L3).

questions.key_step: |z|^2/z = conj z turns the expression into 24 |conj(2z1+3z2+4z3)|
questions.justification: Section formula then the standard z conj z trick, familiar to prepared students; routine chain, nearest 2025-P2-Q13 style complex numerics but easier; 2023-P1-Q11 (L3) is harder.

questions.key_step: Simon's factoring (n-2010)(m-2010)=2010*2009, rule out negative pair, count divisors
questions.justification: Familiar SFFT trick but large numbers, factorisation and sign argument with no options; below 2026-P2-Q6 (L4) factoring question.

questions.key_step: Hand = multiset of 4 values from 13 (stars and bars or 4-case count)
questions.justification: Short casework or one stars-and-bars formula; routine counting; nearest 2021-P2-Q1 (L2).

questions.key_step: r^2+r-1=r(r+1)-1 splits the term as T_{r+1}-T_r with T_r=(r-1)! r!
questions.justification: Telescoping with factorials where the split must be found; easier than 2025-P2-Q15 (L4) because the structure is hinted by the right side 9!10!-1.

questions.key_step: Counting ordered triples of faces with product at most 6, then summing
questions.justification: Six small cases of routine casework (25 triples) with no options to check; no insight needed, but a numerical format leaves a slip risk. Chained routine steps, so 2 not 1.

questions.key_step: Shift of two observations by one class width changes the sum by 20
questions.justification: One familiar move (sum changes by class-mark difference); the variance is a distractor. Easier than the nearest anchor, which needs two unknowns recovered.

questions.key_step: Expand the square and sum the arithmetico-geometric cross term exactly enough to floor
questions.justification: Two chapters; the cross term needs the arithmetico-geometric sum, and the sign of the ratio is a trap. Numerical answer, long exact arithmetic, but each stage is routine. Level 3 beside 2026-P2-Q11.

questions.key_step: Real coefficients give a conjugate pair, fixing which root is real and a=4
questions.justification: Conjugate-root idea plus identifying the real root and a factorisation; the stem as printed is inconsistent (|a+b+c| vs |P(1)|). Two linked ideas, numerical: Level 3, level with 2023-P1-Q11.

questions.key_step: Rays (not lines): tangency needs foot of perpendicular on the ray; both signs of alpha
questions.justification: Argument curves are rays, so tangency must be checked on the ray, and the symmetric second value is easy to miss; two ideas, numerical, no options. Same band as 2021-P1-Q16.

questions.key_step: Translate modulus conditions to parabola and circle, then tangents meeting the axis
questions.justification: Routine chain: loci to conics, intersection, two tangents, one area; no insight needed. Same band as 2026-P2-Q2 (parabola tangent chain, L2).

questions.key_step: Symmetry for P(W>L); adj A=-A means trace 0, then count a^2+bc=1
questions.justification: Two chapters, three stages (multinomial tie count, matrix condition, count), each routine; numerical, no options and slip risk. Printed key is wrong, adding confusion. Level 3, with 2026-P2-Q11.

questions.key_step: Cyclicity of unit digits mod 4, then pairing residue classes
questions.justification: One familiar idea (cyclicity) plus a short residue-class pairing count; routine, no insight. Numerical format only nudges, so 2.

questions.key_step: Rewrite sinθ+i cosθ in cis form and use De Moivre; n ≡ 1 (mod 4)
questions.justification: Short, standard De Moivre rewriting with one congruence step; no insight beyond the usual shift by pi/2. Slightly above the single-formula level 1 anchor.

questions.key_step: Apollonius circle, then cyclic parallelogram is a rectangle with max area 2r^2
questions.justification: Standard Apollonius locus (L1 anchor) plus one extra move (inscribed parallelogram, maximise via diagonals); short chain, no heavy computation.

questions.key_step: Two-state chain gives 4/9 so m=4; then tan^-1 difference formula gives x^4=4
questions.justification: Two chapters linked through m (the problem is only solvable if m is derived); dependent-trial casework, then a standard identity. Chain of routine stages, numerical: Level 3 like 2023-P2-Q3 (ITF) and 2023-P2-Q2 (dependent tosses).

questions.key_step: Probability = angle fraction because the annulus is rotation-symmetric
questions.justification: One familiar move (area ratio of an annular sector); no casework or chain. Comparable to the other one-move numericals at Level 1.

questions.key_step: Glue the block, then notice ABBCABBC is double-counted (overlap correction)
questions.justification: Single block-gluing idea is familiar, but the double-count correction is a precision trap with no options; moderately above routine, below the heavy casework of 2023-P2-Q10.

questions.key_step: Binomial lower bound 2 plus the bound $<e<3$ for the upper side
questions.justification: Routine chain of two standard bounds on $(1+1/n)^n$; no insight beyond a known fact; answer-type numerical. Level 2 (more than a one-move question).

questions.key_step: Split by number of fours (or use the difference of two counts)
questions.justification: A standard single approach with a short sum; one familiar move. Level 1.

questions.key_step: Negative-binomial setup: 4 reds in 12 draws, then red
questions.justification: Standard Bernoulli-trial setup chained with factoring of the result; no options to check. Level 2.

questions.key_step: Treat each error as independent with its own number of surviving checks
questions.justification: The modelling step (independence per error, different exposure times) is not routine, but the arithmetic is short; two ideas linked. Level 3.

questions.key_step: Combined-variance formula with the mean-shift terms $d_i^2$
questions.justification: Standard multi-group variance formula, then arithmetic and reduction check; several routine steps, no insight. Level 2.

questions.key_step: Shift identity $\sum(x_i-c)^2=\sum(x_i-\bar x)^2+n(\bar x-c)^2$, then reject the equal case
questions.justification: Routine chain; one nuance (distinctness excludes a sign). No heavy computation. Level 2, same as 2026-P2-Q12.

questions.key_step: Recognise the alternating even-index series as the real part of $(1+i\tan\theta)^n$ with $\tan15^\circ$
questions.justification: Unfamiliar-looking series; the key idea (De Moivre plus binomial, divide by $\cos^n$, choose $15^\circ$) is not a routine coaching pattern, though execution is short. Numerical, no options. Level 4.

questions.key_step: Inclusion-exclusion on 'some player undefeated' and 'some player winless', counting $A\cap B$ with the shared game
questions.justification: Needs a careful inclusion-exclusion with a shared game in the intersection; one slip changes the answer and there are no options. Two linked ideas. Level 3.

questions.key_step: Decode the game: player $k$ fails with probability $\frac{6-k}{6}$, multiply
questions.justification: One interpretive step then a short product; routine multiplication theorem. Level 2.

questions.key_step: Reduce to $N^2+N+2=2^N$ and find the unique integer root
questions.justification: Short reduction and a trial/graph check; single idea with small execution. Level 2.

questions.key_step: Counting the 5 admissible head/tail sequences with the shared third flip, then 4^3 = 1 mod 7
questions.justification: Short enumeration (5 sequences) plus an easy remainder; two routine stages with no hidden idea and small precision risk. Between 2021-P2-Q17 (L1, single counting move) and 2024-P2-Q9 (L3, set-up needed).

questions.key_step: Reduce to the 3 admissible alpha/beta patterns, then distribute 6 distinct letters into 6 gaps
questions.justification: Needs the pattern-then-gaps decomposition and stars-and-bars on a non-obvious structure; answer is a single digit with no options, so a miscounted pattern is fatal. Similar in demand to 2026-P1-Q11 (L3).

questions.key_step: Each modulus equation is a perpendicular bisector; intersect the two lines
questions.justification: One familiar move (equidistance = perpendicular bisector) applied twice, then solve two linear equations; no insight or casework. Like 2025-P1-Q7 (L1).

questions.key_step: Read numerator and denominator as median vectors; the angle between medians of an equilateral triangle is 120 degrees
questions.justification: One geometric recognition (medians, centroid) after rewriting; short but the idea of reading the ratio as median vectors is only moderately common, so Level 2 not 1. Compare 2025-P2-Q13 (L3, longer) and 2025-P1-Q7 (L1).

questions.key_step: Recognise the roots as non-identity 7th roots of unity and use power-sum values
questions.justification: One standard move (multiply by z-1; roots of unity power sums) applied to three easy sums; no counting or casework. Like 2024-P2-Q3 / 2026-P2-Q4 (one familiar trick, L1).

questions.key_step: Lines through O; cosine rule with the length condition, then AM-GM on OA/OB + OB/OA
questions.justification: Several stages (decode lines, cosine rule, bound by AM-GM) but each is routine; the stem is also garbled, adding reading risk. Compare 2021-P1-Q16 (L3, complex-plane geometry).

questions.key_step: Eliminate z to get P(t)=t(t^2+2004)^2-1 up to a constant, then notice P(-1)<0 when taking the floor
questions.justification: Elimination of z by separating odd and even parts is a moderately known trick, followed by a sign-sensitive floor with no options. Three stages, medium precision risk. Similar to 2023-P1-Q11 (L3).

questions.key_step: Use conj z = 1/z to get the second symmetric function, then solve the cubic
questions.justification: The conjugate-reciprocal trick on unimodular numbers is a familiar move; then a cubic that factorises and an ordering; short routine chain, no casework. Compare 2023-P1-Q11 (L3) as the upper bound; this is lighter.

questions.key_step: Roots-of-unity filter keeps exponents divisible by 7
questions.justification: A single standard filter applied to a polynomial in generic notation, then reading off the surviving exponents; heavier notation than L1 but no insight beyond the trick. Level 2 as a short routine chain.

questions.key_step: Total probability over the number of aces removed (or symmetry: the drawn pair is a uniform random pair)
